items.difficulty_reason: In a domain the lemma identifies associates with generators of a common principal ideal (statement lines 29585-29589). The proof does not need unique factorization: one direction keeps the unit explicit, and the other direction converts the two inclusions (x) contained in (y) and (y) contained in (x) into the two divisibility relations x = fy and y = gx, substitutes to get x = fg x, and cancels the nonzero element x, which is exactly where the domain hypothesis is used (proof lines 29591-29597). The cancellation step is the one that carries the content, and the author writes both directions out. H2.
